title: Compile the exam
subtitle: Private probes for this buyer's traffic — ground truth by construction

text: Parsing the need. The decision-relevant
entities are callback numbers and drug
names — both are dial-back and dosage
risks, so the exam scores exact-match

on those entities, not WER.

Houston
after-hours means Spanish–English code-switching
mid-sentence, cell-phone capture, a
G.711 μ-law PSTN leg at 8 kHz, and front-desk

babble behind the caller.

Sampling
plan: five strata, weighted by harm.
Callback numbers take the largest arm
— one wrong digit dials a stranger.
Each probe is synthesized script → bilingual
TTS → babble at target SNR → band-limit
→ μ-law, so ground truth is known by
construction: we wrote the script.

name: Callback numbers under babble
rationale: You dial these back — a single digit error is a wrong patient at 2am.

name: Drug names + doses, code-switched
rationale: Rx entities flip language mid-utterance; a dose mishear is a safety event.

name: Rapid Spanglish switching
rationale: Houston callers alternate clause-by-clause; monolingual LMs derail here.

name: Low-SNR cell, parking lot
rationale: Worst caller is the sickest caller — 5 dB SNR, wind, μ-law clipping.

name: Disfluent openings + hold music
rationale: Real calls start with hesitation and IVR bleed; benchmarks never do.
